## Discovery & Translational Science

- **Modular synthesis of C5-sulfenyl thiazoles via Pummerer rearrangement** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42604554/)
  - Describes a synthetic route to C5-sulfenyl thiazoles using an intermolecular Pummerer rearrangement.
  - Positions the C5-sulfenyl thiazole framework as an underexplored scaffold for medicinal chemistry development.

- **Redox, inflammasome, and cell-death pathways in antimony and NSAID hepatotoxicity** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42604827/)
  - Maps molecular mechanisms underlying liver injury caused by antimony and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
  - Highlights redox imbalances, inflammasome activation, and programmed cell death as target networks for natural hepatoprotective agents.

- **Cytotoxic diterpenoids isolated from Excoecaria agallocha** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42604695/)
  - Identified diterpenoid compounds extracted from the plant *Excoecaria agallocha*.
  - Evaluated the cytotoxic activity of the isolated diterpenoids in vitro.

- **Bloating as an uncaptured therapeutic endpoint in IBS-C** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42604656/)
  - Examined endpoint discordance in constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-C) trials.
  - Identifies abdominal bloating as a distinct therapeutic signal that is not fully captured by standard regulatory endpoints.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca halts Phase 3 trial of PD-1 × CTLA-4 bispecific in 1L lung cancer** [Brad Loncar on X](https://x.com/bradloncar/status/2089238716783243565)
  - AstraZeneca has stopped its Phase 3 trial evaluating a PD-1 × CTLA-4 bispecific antibody in first-line non-small cell lung cancer due to futility (unconfirmed report via X).

- **[Biotech]** **Efgartigimod IV impact on immature platelet fraction in ITP** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42604730/)
  - Evaluated the effect of intravenous efgartigimod on immature platelet fraction in primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).
  - Utilized patient data from the Phase 3 ADVANCE IV clinical trial.

- **Induction TPF vs. adjuvant PF after CCRT in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42604670/)
  - Conducted a multicenter, randomized controlled Phase 3 trial in patients with locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
  - Compared induction TPF (docetaxel, cisplatin, fluorouracil) against adjuvant PF (cisplatin, fluorouracil) following concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT).

## Business & Strategy

- **State legislation drives drop in private equity physician practice acquisitions** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/17/private-equity-50-percent-drop-physician-practice-management-deals-2026/)
  - Private equity transactions for physician practice management firms are experiencing a sharp decline.
  - Increased state-level legislative oversight is curbing consolidation across medical practice groups.

## Public Health & Policy

- **NIH proposes overhaul of grant peer-review scoring and reporting** [Science-Based Medicine](https://sciencebasedmedicine.org/the-opposite-of-transparency-sneaking-lysenkoism-into-nih-peer-review/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=the-opposite-of-transparency-sneaking-lysenkoism-into-nih-peer-review)
  - An NIH Request for Information (RFI NOT-OD-26-088) outlines proposed changes to how grant peer-review scoring outcomes are reported to applicants under the Unified Funding Strategy.
  - Critics argue the strategy de-emphasizes objective paylines and numerical study-section scores, expanding administrative discretion to override scientific merit rankings based on policy goals.

**Worth watching:** Official confirmation and detailed readout from AstraZeneca regarding the reported Phase 3 futility stop for its 1L NSCLC PD-1 × CTLA-4 bispecific program.

- Biology & Health
    - [404 ‒ Mental health beyond neurotransmitters: hormones in psychiatry, psychedelic therapies, & more](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fs89fhQCfj4) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Dr. Linus Abrams and Dr. Peter Attia discuss evolving psychiatry beyond the classical monoamine hypothesis to incorporate the role of hormones, metabolism, inflammation, circadian biology, and the endocrine system in shaping mood and cognition.
        - Endocrine-driven psychiatric conditions are detailed, including how rapid progesterone drops trigger PMDD and postpartum depression, how hypothyroidism presents clinically as depression, and how chronically elevated cortisol drives hyperarousal.
        - The conversation addresses male and female sex hormone regulation, explaining estradiol's modulating effects on brain neurotransmitters, clarifying the importance of estrogen in men, and evaluating why exogenous testosterone is clinically superior to clomiphene for treating male hypogonadism.
        - Novel and non-traditional interventions for psychiatric illness are examined, focusing on the differential diagnosis between bipolar disorder and unipolar depression, ketamine's efficacy in recalcitrant depression, and the therapeutic potential and clinical cautions surrounding psychedelics like psilocybin.
